book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Stop at sea

parts.note: surface reading: halting a ship out on the ocean
setter's reading: the sailor's own word for stop, an order shouted on board

explanation.walkthrough: This is a plain nautical definition: BELAY is the shipboard command to stop or cease, as in 'belay that order'.
explanation.definitionFit: In naval slang the command means cease or halt, so it is the seafaring word for stop.

clue.text: Protection for king caught in an intriguing situation

indicators.note: something caught in something else is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an amour is a secret love affair, an intrigue
R, from Latin rex, is the usual abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch caught up in a plot needs something to shield him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intriguing' here means having an illicit affair, not fascinating; ARMOUR is AMOUR with R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour is metal or plating that shields a body or vehicle from harm, a kind of protection.

clue.text: Nevertheless last

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in spite of everything
second meaning: coming after every other one, finally

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the phrase means behind everyone else, which is last; as an idiom it means nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses concession, like nevertheless, while literally it describes a position behind every other, which is last.

clue.text: It gives the retired member a warm feeling

definitions.text: It gives the retired member a warm feeling

parts.words: the retired member a warm feeling
parts.note: surface reading: a pensioner or former club member made to feel welcome
setter's reading: a limb of someone who has retired to bed, namely a foot

explanation.surface: Something gives a former club member a glow of warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' means gone to bed and 'member' means a limb, so the thing warms a foot in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsock is a soft sock worn in bed to keep the feet warm at night.

clue.text: Yet he enjoys some standing at meetings

definitions.text: Yet he enjoys some standing at meetings

parts.words: he enjoys some standing at meetings
parts.note: surface reading: someone who is on his feet at gatherings
setter's reading: he has status, even though he is the one who sits in the seat of honour

explanation.surface: Someone, oddly, likes to stand up at meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' means rank, not being on one's feet; 'Yet' marks the paradox that the person who has it is the one seated in the chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who presides over a meeting sits in its chair yet holds the most authority in the room.

clue.text: Soap, water — what next?

parts.note: surface reading: someone asking what comes after soap and water when washing, a towel perhaps
setter's reading: soap and water give cleanliness, and the proverb says what comes next to it

explanation.surface: Someone working through a wash asks what comes after the soap and water.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'cleanliness is next to godliness' is the key: soap and water stand for cleanliness, so what sits next to it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying puts piety beside personal cleanliness, so the quality named after it is holiness or devotion.

clue.text: Scared of fire, tried to put it out

indicators.note: putting something out disturbs it, and a fire put out is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frightened of flames nonetheless had a go at extinguishing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being terrified is being extremely frightened, a stronger synonym of scared.

clue.text: Laughter in company's causing confusion

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, with the S of the possessive
ha is the sound of a laugh

explanation.surface: Giggling in the firm's office leads to disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe S counts as a letter, so the company abbreviation becomes a three-letter wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is total disorder, so it is a stronger synonym for confusion.

clue.text: It's capital using mail order

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them again, so these letters get a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mail order makes a fortune, a capital idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail order' looks like one business phrase, but 'order' works alone on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Her rank prohibits one's admission

definitions.note: names the title a woman holds; the answer is the title

indicators.note: an admission lets something in, so one piece is let inside the other

parts.note: to bar is to prohibit
one with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A woman's high status forbids letting a particular person in.
explanation.walkthrough: BARS takes in ONES: BAR-ONES-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroness is a title of nobility held by a woman, the rank she bears in the peerage.

clue.text: Eavesdropper of low degree

parts.note: surface reading: a lowly snoop listening in on others
setter's reading: something that drops from the eaves of a roof
setter's reading: at a low temperature, below freezing

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as eaves-dropper, a thing that hangs and drips from the eaves, and 'low degree' becomes a cold temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle hangs from roof edges and forms only when the temperature is below freezing.

clue.text: Time to return to a region

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way one came, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is time to go back to a certain part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'to' is a joiner: the reversed period is followed by A.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a district or stretch of land, the same thing as a region.

clue.text: In which the workers unpicked seams

definitions.text: In which the workers unpicked seams

parts.note: surface reading: a garment workshop where tailors unstitch seams
setter's reading: miners work layers of mineral in the rock with picks

explanation.surface: A sewing room where the staff took the stitching out of seams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unpicked' suggests unpicking stitches, but here it means worked with a pick, and seams are layers of mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit is where miners dig out underground seams of fuel, traditionally with picks.

clue.text: Critical of racialist broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast once meant scattering seed widely, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of a bigoted programme on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Satirical writing mocks its targets, so it is critical in tone.

clue.text: The form in which astronauts take their medicine?

definitions.text: The form in which astronauts take their medicine?

parts.words: The form in which astronauts take their medicine
parts.note: surface reading: how space crews swallow their pills
setter's reading: the small craft that carries astronauts, which shares its name with a pill

explanation.walkthrough: One word serves both as a pill and as the cabin of a spacecraft; 'take their medicine' also means accept their risks.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsule is a dissolving shell holding a dose of a drug, and also the crew compartment of a spacecraft.

clue.text: This man advertises food and old port

definitions.meaning: first meaning: two slices of bread around a filling
second meaning: a town in Kent, one of the medieval Cinque Ports, now silted up

explanation.surface: A man promotes snacks and a historic harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This man advertises' is a third hint: a sandwich man walks the street wearing advertising boards front and back.
explanation.definitionFit: The snack is named after the Earl of Sandwich, whose title comes from the Kent town that was a leading port.

clue.text: A grand player, perhaps, from his score

parts.note: surface reading: a top sportsman

parts.words: grand player, perhaps, from his score
parts.note: setter's reading: someone playing a grand piano, reading his musical score

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' is the piano, not excellence, and 'score' is written music rather than points in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist plays the piano, often a grand, reading from printed sheet music.

clue.text: Asks how paper may be sold

definitions.note: a phrase, read as two words IN QUIRES
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in bundles of 24 or 25 sheets, the old unit of sale for writing paper

explanation.surface: Someone wants to know how stationery is sold.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper, so paper is sold 'in quires'.
explanation.definitionFit: To inquire is to ask, seeking information by putting a question.

clue.text: Cinders gets the wicked dame feeling guilty

parts.note: cinders and ash are both the residue of a fire

indicators.note: something wicked is twisted or bent, so the word after it is distorted

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cinderella faces the wicked stepmother of pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinders is Cinderella in British pantomime, where the villains are wicked; here it simply means ash.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ashamed is to feel guilt or embarrassment over something one has done.

clue.text: Nice safe sort of girls to marry

indicators.note: to sort something is to arrange it, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pleasant, reliable young women make good brides.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiancées are women engaged to be married, the girls someone plans to wed.

clue.text: Limits one's ambitions

explanation.surface: Someone sets bounds on what they hope to achieve.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the extremities of something and the purposes one is working towards.

clue.text: A pound of tobacco?

parts.note: surface reading: a weight of 454 grams of tobacco
setter's reading: the slang word for a pound sterling, which is also a plug of chewing tobacco

explanation.walkthrough: The word is British slang for a pound in money and also a lump of tobacco for chewing.
explanation.definitionFit: The same short slang word names a pound coin and a wad of chewing tobacco, so it answers both readings.

clue.text: Rapid inflow in basket material

parts.note: taken as written
rushes are reeds woven into baskets and mats

explanation.surface: Water floods into a woven basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a preposition joining the two halves, but it supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An inrush is a sudden flooding in, a fast influx of water, air or people.

clue.text: It's said in France to be the same

parts.note: dit is French for said
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French expression supposedly means 'to be identical'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said in France' asks for the French word, not a sound effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to say that the same thing applies again, as with ditto marks in a list.

clue.text: Watched United compete to get the lead

parts.note: to vie is to compete
wed means joined in marriage

explanation.surface: A spectator saw United battle to go in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get the lead' tells you the compete piece goes in front of the united piece. United looks like a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To view something is to look at it, so viewed means watched.

clue.text: Number to help out with sound rule for pollution

indicators.note: put to something means placed into it, so the first piece goes inside the next

parts.note: to help someone out is to aid them
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: sound tells you the word is used for how it is said, not how it is written

parts.note: a reign is a monarch's rule

explanation.surface: A figure supports a vigorous anti-pollution law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number to help out' means the number is put into the help word; 'sound' marks only the rule word, the monarch's term of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is rainfall made acidic by industrial emissions, a well-known form of pollution.

clue.text: Trap door fastener

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to snare or capture
second meaning: a latch or hook that keeps a door shut

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap door' reads as a hatch in a floor, but the two words split: 'Trap' is one meaning, 'door fastener' the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for seizing something and a noun for a small device that holds a door closed.

clue.text: Must it end in tragedy following extraordinary scenes?

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of tragedy

explanation.surface: A theatre-goer wonders whether such dramatic scenes must end tragically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' means IT and Y come after the rearranged scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: A must is something essential or unavoidable, which is what a necessity is.
